FSP uprev checklist — the files that carry FSP code or FSP values

Some files in the port exist only to bridge FSP to TF-M. They carry FSP code, restate an FSP-generated value, or depend on an FSP internal, but they are not FSP files: regenerating the e2 projects does not update them, and nothing in the build compares them against their origin. They drift on an FSP pack uprev, and the failure is a stale constant that links cleanly and is wrong at run time.

Work through this before the uprev, not after. Every item below names something you can run or an assertion that fires. <part> is ra6m5 or ra8m2 throughout.

The port ships on FSP 6.7.0-beta0, so a move to the release pack is the first uprev a customer will make.

Four drifts of this kind have already happened. FLASH_AREA_IMAGE_SECTOR_SIZE was 0x1000 in the RA8M2 flash_layout.h while the generated mcuboot_config.h had 0x8000, which made slots 9.875 sectors long and failed only on hardware. Two CMake files hardcoded the sce9 engine directory on a part whose engine directory is rsip_e50d. config.cmake asserted BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_SCE9_SUPPORTED == 1 on a part where it is 0. An 87-line Protected Storage comment described a data flash that the part does not have.

1. The Mbed TLS patch set

Each part carries five patches in platform/ext/target/renesas/<part>/mbedtls/. Four of them — 0003, 0004, 0006 and 0007 — are TF-M's own patches rebased onto the FSP Mbed TLS tree. They match lib/ext/mbedcrypto/ in content but differ in commit hash, blob index and hunk offset, so a plain file comparison always reports a difference and tells you nothing.

Compare them with the From, index and @@ lines removed. A difference in the remaining lines means TF-M changed the patch and the rebased copy has not followed; read it and rebase.

0100-FSP-fit-TF-M-config-file-name-and-owner-key-ids.patch is port-specific, has no upstream counterpart, and differs between the two parts. Compare it only against the previous revision of the same part.

The four shared patches are byte-identical between RA6M5 and RA8M2, which makes comparing the two parts a cheap cross-check.

2. The generated MCUboot sector size

findstr RM_MCUBOOT_MRAM_BLOCK_SIZE ra8m2_gcc_mcuboot\ra_cfg\mcu-tools\include\mcuboot_config\mcuboot_config.h

It must still equal FLASH_AREA_IMAGE_SECTOR_SIZE in <part>/flash_layout.h.

This one cannot be machine-checked, which is why it needs a manual step. FSP hardcodes the value rather than deriving it from a BSP_FEATURE macro, and the same generated header also defines FLASH_AREA_IMAGE_SECTOR_SIZE, so it cannot be included alongside the port's copy to compare. What <part>_layout_checks.c does assert is that the part reports the memory type it expects and that the sector is a whole number of write units.

3. struct flash_area — a guard collision with no diagnostic

The highest-consequence drift surface in the port, because nothing in the build signals it.

TF-M's bl2/ext/mcuboot/include/flash_map/flash_map.h and the FSP rm_mcuboot_port/flash_map_backend/flash_map_backend.h both use the include guard H_UTIL_FLASH_MAP_, so whichever is reached first suppresses the other silently. They do not define the same type: TF-M's is 16 bytes and carries an extra ARM_DRIVER_FLASH *fa_driver between pad16 and fa_off, where the FSP one is 12 bytes without it. With the wrong definition in bootutil, every member after pad16 is read one slot late. Both are complete types, the link succeeds, and the only symptom is a bootloader that rejects a correct image.

Both parts compile TF-M's struct, and neither builds rm_mcuboot_port into the secure or bootloader image. The FSP header is nevertheless still on an include path — the bootloader project's generated hal_data.h includes rm_mcuboot_port.h, which includes bootutil/image.h — so the collision is avoided by scope rather than by absence. Those paths are private to the BSP bootloader library and never reach bootutil.

The check: every bootutil and flash_map object must report 16 bytes.

arm-none-eabi-readelf --debug-dump=info <build>\bl2\...\<object>.o

Look for the flash_area structure type and its DW_AT_byte_size. Scope the check to bootutil and flash_map objects: a BSP bootloader object reporting 12 is expected and is not a failure. A bootutil object reporting 12 means the FSP header has reached the bootutil include path. A stale object on disk can report either size, so confirm the object is still in the build before chasing it.

An FSP uprev that adds a member to its struct, or a TF-M bump that changes TF-M's, breaks this again with no warning.

4. The rm_psa_crypto tree

Compare the FSP ra/fsp/src/rm_psa_crypto/ tree in a regenerated project against the previous pack. Of its 35 files only aes_alt.c and cipher_alt.c have ever differed between the two engine packs the port has used, so this comparison is high signal at almost no cost.

5. The accelerator source list

The accelerator CMakeLists.txt selects a subset of the *_alt.c sources FSP ships, with CCM excluded deliberately. FSP adding, removing or fixing a source does not change that list, and two session-leak fixes were nearly missed this way. After an uprev, list the FSP *_alt.c files and compare them against the list.

The inventory, grouped by how each drifts

The exclusion keeps applying after FSP changes the original, so nothing complains.

bsp_init_stub.cthe FSP init, copy and nocache tables, and the g_main_stack aliasthe alias is asserted as S_MSP_STACK_SIZE == BSP_CFG_STACK_MAIN_BYTES + STACKSEAL_SIZE

Depends on an FSP internal rather than its public API

FSP may refactor something it never promised to keep. A link error is the good outcome; the bad one is a signature that still matches with changed semantics.

FileDepends on
cmsis_drivers/Driver_Flash.cthe erase block units and the InfoGet field layout of the part's flash driver. It also declares the generated instance objects directly rather than including ra_gen/hal_data.h, which would pull in the FSP psa/crypto.h and shadow TF-M's for the whole secure platform library
ra_sce_init.cHW_SCE_McuSpecificInit(), a private adapter primitive
sce_trng.cHW_SCE_RNG_Read(), likewise
the accelerator crypto_hw.cpsa_aead_setup_vendor(), declared locally in both engine trees
<part>_fsp_sections.icfthe FSP section names

Shadows an FSP module wholesale

rm_mcuboot_port, bsp_linker.c, and startup.c with ra_gen/main.c. Each carries its reason in the file.

rm_psa_crypto and ra/arm/mbedtls are a narrower case: the port excludes the FSP PSA core module build and its Mbed TLS config, not the FSP crypto code. The *_ALT sources come from platform/ext/accelerator/renesas/<engine> and the library from the Mbed TLS overlay, so §4 and §5 treat those sources as part of the image, which is correct.

The SCE module is not shadowed at all: it is built for the secure and bootloader roles, and is removed only from the non-secure glob, which is a different image. ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md §2 sets the three exclusion mechanisms side by side; they are easy to confuse, and only two of them exclude anything.

The option-memory family — the highest-consequence case

The failure mode is not a build error. Take the worked hazard: a user changes an option setting in e2, rebuilds, and expects the new value to be programmed.

StageComes fromWhat goes wrong silently
the valuesthe bootloader project's ra_cfg/.../bsp_mcu_ofs_cfg.hedited in the secure project instead, which has no effect and gives no warning. bl2_option_setting.c compiles into the bootloader platform library, so only the bootloader project is on the path, and both projects define the same groups
the addressesthe bootloader project's generated Debug/memory_regions.*, filtered into option_settings.h at configure timeRA8M2 derives them. RA6M5 still transcribes them by hand, which is the open back-port
which groups existthe device. FSP emits a BSP_CFG_OPTION_SETTING_* only for what the user seta group enabled in e2 that the port does not place is dropped with no diagnostic
the placement<part>_bl2.ld and <part>_bl2.icfone coalesced load segment zero-fills the span between the emitted words, writing 0x00 into eight defined option registers and the reserved bytes between them. That made two EK-RA6M4 boards un-erasable and no recovery is known. It is invisible in the srec

Each hazard has a mechanism rather than a comment:

  • bl2_option_setting.c ends in a guard listing every option word FSP knows for the part that the port does not place. Any of them being set stops the build with the three edits it needs. RA8M2 carries 22 of these guards and RA6M5 none, which is the same open back-port.
  • check_ofs.py requires its address window to be passed. It used to hardcode the RA6 window, and against an RA8M2 bootloader carrying six option segments it printed CLEAN (no OFS segments) … safe to flash. A guard pointed at the wrong window is worse than none, because it reads as verification. The bootloader check also passes --require-segments, so an empty result fails.
  • readelf -l on the linked ELF is the only place the coalescing is visible. GETTING_STARTED.md §6 has the pre-flash form of both checks.

bsp_linker.cexcluded. Its jobs are reimplemented in bl2_option_setting.c and bsp_init_stub.c on both parts, plus ra8m2_ddsc.c on RA8M2
Debug/fsp_gen.{ld,icf}, script/fsp.{ld,icf}unused, because TF-M supplies its own. Worth keeping as the reference for what FSP would have done: they were the source of the discrete-region pattern
